subject: EU-South planned maintenance — staged safe-swap guidance
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.example.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0400
Subject: EU-South planned maintenance — staged safe-swap guidance

Hi Tom,

We wanted to give you an early heads-up about a planned maintenance window affecting the eu-south region on Monday, 28 June. This will be a staged driver/kernel swap with rolling restarts across availability zones; the primary goals are to apply a driver compatibility fix and restore a small number of hosts that have been failing KV cache warmup more frequently.

High level:
- Window: 2027-06-28 02:00 — 06:00 UTC (staged per-zone cadence)
- Expected per-zone disruption: brief pod drains followed by node restart (10–15 minutes of elevated tail latency for in-flight requests, no planned data-plane downtime)
- Mitigations: prefix KV cache preservation, automatic fallback to compatible model variant if warm cache misses persist, and prioritized traffic routing to unaffected hosts.

We attach a short maintenance_summary.pdf and the planned_node_list.csv so you can see which hosts may be touched. Recommended customer actions:
- Avoid scheduling large inference batch runs in eu-south between 01:30 — 07:00 UTC on Jun 28 if possible.
- If you must run, please mark those jobs as lower-priority and expect transient latency spikes.

If you have time-sensitive workloads (backups, scheduled nightly jobs, bulk embedding runs), reply with the job times and we will coordinate a targeted exclusion or additional buffering. We will also publish the maintenance start on Status and provide a realtime update channel.

Follow-ups: we will send an updated note 24 hours and 2 hours before the window, and a postmortem once we've validated the rollout.

Thanks,
Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Sr. Infrastructure PM, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.example.com
+1 (415) 555-0139

Attachments: maintenance_summary.pdf (summary), planned_node_list.csv (node ids)

From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@acme-cloud.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.example.com>
Cc: infra-ops@acme-cloud.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:17:00 +0100
Subject: Re: EU-South planned maintenance — staged safe-swap guidance

Thanks for the heads-up, Mina — appreciate the level of detail. Two quick asks from our side:

1) We have a daily batch embedding job that starts at 03:30 UTC and runs ~90 minutes. Can you confirm whether the zone our instances sit in will be scheduled early or late in the window? If it's early, we may need you to exclude our node pool or confirm failover.

2) Do you have a short runbook we can share with our SREs (expected symptoms, timeouts to look for, recommended client-side retry policy)?

On the embed job: we can delay it if needed, but we need at least 6 hours notice. Call me if you want to triage — Tom (mobile: +44 7700 900123).

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:40:00 -0400
Subject: RE: EU-South planned maintenance — staged safe-swap guidance

Mina / Grace —

We can handle an exclusion for Acme's node pool if they provide the node tags, but two flags to note:
- We currently plan to rotate zones in the order eu-south-1a -> 1b -> 1c starting at 02:00 UTC. If Acme's instances are in 1a, that would hit around 02:10 UTC (early in the window).
- We can expand the advertised buffer to 01:30—07:00 UTC for customers that need extra breathing room, but that increases our risk of overlap with other region operations later in the week.

Action items:
- Mina: please ask Tom to send node tags / cluster names. We can add an exclusion rule and confirm the exclusion no later than 24 hours before start.
- Grace: can you prepare a one-page runbook (client symptoms, example retry headers, recommended backoff) — we can attach that to the outbound notice.

Forwarded for context: Tom's reply (below).

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.example.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.example.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 12:06:00 -04:00
Subject: RE: EU-South planned maintenance — staged safe-swap guidance

Tom — thanks for the quick reply. Two quick updates and concrete next steps:

1) Window extension: we will expand the buffer and mark the maintenance advisory broadly as 2027-06-28 01:30 — 07:00 UTC to give customers who need it a safe margin.

2) Exclusion and runbook: please send the Acme node tags / cluster names to infra-ops@acme-cloud.com (copy me) and we will add an exclusion rule for your pool. Grace has drafted a short runbook; attaching customer_runbook.md with symptom examples (HTTP 504, large tail latencies, cache-warm misses), recommended client retry windows (exponential backoff up to 30s), and an example health-check snippet.

If you prefer we can coordinate a one-off maintenance exclusion rather than a full exclusion; tell us your cluster name and preferred exclusion window and we'll confirm within 6 hours.

We will post the 24-hour and 2-hour notices to https://status.redwood.com and create a live update thread in the existing ticket HUBSPOT-98765. A postmortem will be published within 5 business days after completion; if you want an accelerated postmortem, we can prioritize your account.

Point of contact during the window: Rishi Malhotra (infra ops), +1 (415) 555-0192; backup: Marissa Cole (CS), +1 (415) 555-0147.

Thanks — let us know the node tags and we'll take it from there.

Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Sr. Infrastructure PM, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.example.com

Attachments: customer_runbook.md (runbook)
